value.text: RCIN 919027: notes on the death and dissection of an old man

claims.statement: RCIN 919027 (recto veins of the left arm, young and old vessels compared; verso notes on the dissection of an old man and changes in hepatic vessels in old age) records that an old man who said he was over a hundred years old died in the hospital of Santa Maria Nuova and that Leonardo dissected him 'to see the cause of so sweet a death'.

sources.cite: Royal Collection Trust, collection online, RCIN 919027, The veins of the arm and notes on the death of a centenarian, c.1508. Read through search engine excerpts in this session; the page itself was not fetched in this session.

claims.statement: RCT exhibition pages place the dissection in the winter of 1507 to 1508. The note itself, as excerpted, gives no date.

sources.cite: Royal Collection Trust, exhibition page, The Centenarian: Anatomical Manuscript B. Read through search engine excerpts in this session; the page itself was not fetched in this session.

claims.statement: Another page cited by search gives 1506 for the dissection.

sources.cite: University of Melbourne news article on Leonardo's anatomy. Read through search engine excerpts in this session; the page itself was not fetched in this session.

value.text: Dissection of a child of two years

claims.statement: The notes also mention the dissection of a child of two, in whom he found everything contrary to the old man.
